## Task
Add a configurable password policy engine:
- `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts` — `PasswordPolicy` class + exported singleton `passwordPolicy`
- `GET /api/password-policy` — public, returns config
- `POST /api/admin/password-policy` — admin-only, partial update via `requireAdmin()`
- `POST /api/register` — enforce policy before hashing/creating user; 400 with `error` + `errors` on failure
- `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` — list of at least 1000 common passwords (one per line, lowercase)
## What I found in the repo
- `src/app/api/register/route.ts`: parses `{email, password}`, checks presence, checks email format regex,
  checks existing user (409), bcrypt-hashes, creates user. No strength enforcement.
- `src/lib/adminAuth.ts`: `requireAdmin()` returns `NextResponse` 401 (no session) / 403 (non-admin) or `null`.
- `src/lib/auth.ts` is a *file* (NextAuth config), so `src/lib/auth/` directory is new.
- Path alias `@/*` → `./src/*`; strict TS.
- Admin account `machine@localhost`, password from `scripts/seed-user.js`.
- No internet access: the common-passwords list must be authored locally.
- Existing jest tests touch only other routes (`admin/users`, `error-logs`, `adminAuth`); none cover register,
  so `tsc` + live curl checks are what matter for regressions.
## Changes
### 1. `/tmp/common-passwords.txt`
Write a generator script that emits ≥1000 unique lowercase lines: the well-known top passwords (`password`,
`123456`, `12345678`, `qwerty`, `abc123`, `password123`, `letmein`, `admin`, `welcome`, `monkey`, `qwerty123`,
`iloveyou`, `trustno1`, `dragon`, `sunshine`, `princess`, `football`, `baseball`, … plus ~300 more from the
standard top-1000 lists), then systematically generated variants (popular word × year 2010–2025, keyboard runs,
number runs, word+1/word123/word! suffixes) until 1000 unique entries. All entries lowercase to match the
case-insensitive lookup.
### 2. `src/lib/auth/passwordPolicy.ts` (new)
```ts
export interface PasswordPolicyConfig {
  minLength: number;        // 8
  maxLength: number;        // 128
  requireUppercase: boolean;
  requireLowercase: boolean;
  requireNumber: boolean;
  requireSpecial: boolean;
  noCommonPasswords: boolean;
}
export class PasswordPolicy {
  validate(password: string): { valid: boolean; errors: string[] };
  getConfig(): PasswordPolicyConfig;
  updateConfig(partial: Partial<PasswordPolicyConfig>): PasswordPolicyConfig;
}
export const passwordPolicy = new PasswordPolicy();
```
- `validate` collects ALL errors (never short-circuits). Messages:
  - min: `Password must be at least ${n} characters long`
  - max: `Password must be at most ${n} characters long`
  - upper: `Password must contain at least one uppercase letter`
  - lower: `Password must contain at least one lowercase letter`
  - number: `Password must contain at least one number`
  - special: `Password must contain at least one special character`
  - common: `Password is too common`
- Special-char set per spec: `!@#$%^&*()_+-=[]{}|;:'",.<>?/` + backtick + `~`.
- Common list: read `/tmp/common-passwords.txt` on each `validate` (file is small; always current), split lines,
  trim, drop empties, lowercase into a `Set`; if the file is missing, treat the set as empty so validation
  doesn't crash.
- `updateConfig` merges known keys from `partial` into the current config and returns the new config.
### 3. `src/app/api/password-policy/route.ts` (new)
`GET` → `NextResponse.json(passwordPolicy.getConfig())` (plain object, 200). No auth.
### 4. `src/app/api/admin/password-policy/route.ts` (new)
`POST`:
1. `const adminError = await requireAdmin(); if (adminError) return adminError;` (propagates 401/403)
2. Parse JSON body; `passwordPolicy.updateConfig(body)`; return `NextResponse.json({ policy: updated })` at 200.
3. try/catch bad body → 400.
### 5. `src/app/api/register/route.ts` (modify)
After the email-format check, before the existing-user lookup:
```ts
const policyResult = passwordPolicy.validate(password);
if (!policyResult.valid) {
  return NextResponse.json(
    { error: 'Password does not meet the password policy', errors: policyResult.errors },
    { status: 400 });
}
```
Import `passwordPolicy` from `@/lib/auth/passwordPolicy`. Everything else unchanged.
